text:
**LiFePO4 (LFP) is the better choice for most people.** The guides in your search results agree on this.

| | LiFePO4 | NMC |
|---|---|---|
| Cycle life | About 3,000–6,000 cycles | About 1,000–2,000 cycles |
| Safety | More thermally stable and less prone to thermal runaway | Higher fire risk if damaged or abused |
| Weight | Heavier | About 20% lighter for the same capacity |
| Cost | Usually a bit more per unit, but cheaper over its lifespan | Often cheaper upfront or in small, light units |

The cycle-life and weight figures come from [PowerStationMatch](https://powerstationmatch.com/learn/lifepo4-vs-nmc). [Unplugged Watts](https://www.unpluggedwatts.com/lifepo4-vs-nmc-power-station/) also concludes that LiFePO4 is the better buy for most people. [Enough Watts](https://enoughwatts.com/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc) notes that all 54 power stations in its data set use LiFePO4. That suggests NMC is now uncommon in full-size units.

**Choose LiFePO4 if you:**
- Want a home backup, an RV or van, or a unit you'll use or cycle often.
- Plan to keep it for 10 years or more.
- Will store it in a garage or hot environment, or care most about safety.

**Choose NMC only if you:**
- Need the lightest possible unit for backpacking, flying, or frequent carrying.
- Will use it only occasionally, so cycle life matters less.
- Find a much lower price and accept the shorter lifespan.
